newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican rebels put all forces on alert after battles.
newsitem.headline: Mexican rebels put all forces on alert after battles.

text.p: Mexico's Popular Revolutionary Army guerrillas placed all their units on alert following this week's clashes with the army in western Mexico, the rebel group said in a statement.

The Marxist group's military command called the alert amid an army sweep in search of rebels that came after guerrillas and troops fought several times in western Guerrero state, in battles that claimed at least nine lives.

"...The (EPR) military command ... orders a general alert to all its military units in the national territory to be ready to carry out any orders from central command," said the statement dated May 29 and obtained by Reuters on Saturday.
The group said it had no intention of disrupting upcoming mid-term elections in July, accusing the government instead of raising pre-electoral tension.
Rebels said they would continue to carry out peaceful acts of "armed propaganda," fighting the army only if provoked.
The statement, made available in the southern state of Oaxaca, was datelined "Mexican Republic" and gave no hint as to the location of the EPR's military command.
Mexico's leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) on Saturday called on the army to stop hunting rebels and asked the EPR to call a ceasefire ahead of the July 6 poll.
Gen. Afredo Oropeza Garnica, head of Guerrero's 27th Military Region, told PRD lawmakers on Saturday that the army had orders to hunt down the EPR using all possible means.

Leticia Burgos Ochoa, a PRD legislator, said Oropeza told her the military would not call off its anti-insurgency drive. She also confirmed media reports the general had been shot in the arm during the recent battles.
Hundreds of army troops have blocked roads leading in and out of the remote mountainous region where battles erupted, some 40 miles (60 km) north of the Pacific resort of Acapulco.
Armoured vehicles outfitted with machine guns have also fanned out across the area, backed by army helicopters.

Army paratroopers in the past few days have landed in more remote villages of the region, prompting some families to temporarily leave the villages to stay with relatives in other towns, Mexican newspaper La Jornada said on Saturday.
